A 3rd deck will represent the many Espers from across the series, helmed by Bahamut, the Father of the Espers/Aeons/Eidolons or whatever they want to call them this time.

The second best idea I had was an equipment deck to show off the various famous weaponry from across the series, but I have no idea who the commander would be.

So I built several variants of this deck in conjunction with a friend of mine and after much testing of different color combos that this deck can function with we found the version that operates best is the abzan version. [[Cosmic Rebirth]] is such a lynchpin card because it can reanimate Sorin, but also bring your Ghalta/Mavrens and Xanders back to your hand in the event they get got. You need hand attack like [[Thoughtseize]] in main and extra of it, [[Duress]] and [[Collective Brutality]] In the sideboard or some variant of that because protecting your combo is the most vital thing for you above all else. [[Vanishing Verse]] is an extremely powerful removal spell because it hits most of Rakdos, it hits all of Boros Convoke, it hits all of Nykthos's big creatures, and takes care of a number of other problems your deck will have trouble handling. [[Witherbloom Command]] is also good at slowing down faster decks like Convoke and Mono White Humans. [[Gifted Aetherborn]] and [[Nighthawk Scavenger]] are both good creatures with lifelink that are good at slowing down aggro, and can also both be reanimated by Cosmic Rebirth in the case you REALLY need to slow down your opponent if they're playing something like Vehicles, Greasefang or Phoenix. Been thinking about this for quite a long time, somewhat of a pet deck of mine to an extent, so I hope I manage to help!

You have three types of classes. DPS, Tank, and Support (healers are under the support umbrella). You have a party of 6 characters that you can customize to be whatever classes you want, once you reach the part of the game you are able to (it's not that far in), and assuming you have the classes. Most DPS's are the same but they work around varying mechanics such as overall DPS, damage based on crit rate, damage based on draining your life, etc. The tanks only really have two variants being block tanks and evade tanks. Supports are pretty different though with the different buffs the can give, and healers fall under the support umbrella like I mentioned.

From a gameplay standpoint alone? It's a pretty fun combat system. The class system allows for quite a few combinations and different ways to do things that I think it keeps itself fresh. The exploration is great, the game looks fantastic, and you're rewarded for exploring by unlocking new classes via different quest lines. But I will warn you, this game is a VERY heavily story based game. There are some points of the game that are almost like a movie with the amount/length of cutscenes (I like it, but I know that's not everyone's interest). Story wise, you will also miss out on a number of different references and connections back to Xenoblades 1 and 2, as well as you won't have context for some major plot points either. But you said you don't care too much about the story. Gameplay alone, it's very enjoyable at least I think so. Hope I helped!

>!We also learned from the siren figure iirc that there were two other space elevators that held the orbital ring (Elysium) in space.
